h: Answering the Divine Call With Preparation and Humility

p: but to the prophets of the nations of the world
with an expression of happenstance and impurity,
that every utterance and every command
through a gezeirah shavah from the Burning Bush;
is an expression of affection, an expression of urging;
and afterward it says, another explanation:
he was the same before He spoke with him
as he was after He spoke with him.
Now this needs to be understood:
was handed down as a halachah l'Moshe mi'Sinai
in order to teach us something;
so what does this come to teach us,
that there was a calling before every utterance?
This is like the question the Gemara raises (Yoma 5b);
and although we do find such a question
"The ox at Sinai, by how many judges?",
Tosafos there already raised the difficulty.
all words of Torah are eternal
for they are a lesson for man,
is that it comes to teach us
that the main thing on the part of man
as Rashi writes in his commentary
עַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (יִתְרוֹ, שְׁמוֹת יט, א)
"On this day they came to the Wilderness of Sinai":
So that words of Torah should be
as if they were given today.
before the Giving of the Torah,
only that they arrived at the place
where they would afterward receive the Torah,
and that was the preparation for the Giving of the Torah;
and about this preparation he said
a renewed desire for words of Torah.
called "Who gives the Torah," in the present tense;
and about Torah she'b'al peh it is written
"My words which I have placed in your mouth,"
in the heart of Yisrael and in their mouths.
the sum of the entire Torah
"And they shall prepare that which they bring,"
invited to the place that is called Kodesh,
as is stated in the holy Zohar
But the calling and the preparation
הוּא גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
are also from Hashem Yisbarach's side,
for He places desire in the heart of Yisrael;
for calling a person by name
is an awakening of the soul,
as is stated in the writings of the Arizal,
that a person's name being called
is the root of his nefesh chayah;
and therefore he wakes from sleep
when he is called by his name,
And all the more so when Hashem Yisbarach
then at that moment there is added within him
"And as for the dream being repeated twice,
it is because the matter is set, etc.,
and God is hastening to do it."
And this is what is learned here:
that every utterance requires a calling
a preparation on man's part to receive,
so that he be a vessel prepared
and fit for holiness to rest upon him;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּנְבִיאֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
which is not so with the prophets of the nations of the world,
fit and prepared for holiness to rest upon it;
nevertheless in the essence of his soul
he was full of the filth of impurity,
and the speech of prophecy from the Shechinah
as is stated in the holy Zohar
the term "calling" does not apply to him.
And something of this influx of holy abundance
flows to the souls of Yisrael
And this is the "expression of urging, expression of affection"
the affection brings about the urgency,
for one who loves is eager
to do the will of his beloved.
מֹשֶׁה מֹשֶׁה הוּא עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִדְבַּר עִמּוֹ
"Moshe, Moshe": he was the same before He spoke with him
as he was after He spoke with him.
That is, this refers to humility;
that it is an expression of affection and urging,
for the one brings the other, as was said;
he had the trait of love,
and he had the trait of alacrity,
"It teaches us the alacrity of Avraham."
that it is an expression of humility;
And this is based on what they said
that I bestow greatness upon you,
and he said, 'I am but dust and ashes.'"
The greatness that it lists afterward,
which He gave to Nimrod and to Nevuchadnetzar,
and as for Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
אַף שֶׁזָּכָה לִגְדוּלָּה זוֹ גַּם כֵּן
although he too merited this greatness,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה, לֶךְ לְךָ מג, ה)
as they said (Bereishis Rabbah, Lech Lecha 43:5):
אַךְ זֶה לֹא נֶחְשַׁב אֶצְלוֹ לִמְאוּמָה
yet this counted for nothing in his eyes,
that all the nations of the world agreed together
But here, where he accomplished something
through his words and his prayer,
this was a greatness of his own,
that he was esteemed in the eyes of the Omnipresent, blessed be He;
אָז אָמַר הִנֵּה נָא הוֹאַלְתִּי וְגוֹ׳
then he said, "Behold now, I have presumed, etc.,
and I am but dust and ashes,"
for he grasped his own lowliness,
that this power was not from his own side
And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
for what was said of Moshe, etc., is greater
than what was said of Avraham,
as they said in the Gemara (ibid.).
no existence whatsoever in his own eyes,
and he knew that he was only
וְהָיָה זֶה רַק בִּבְחִירַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and that this was only by the choice of Hashem Yisbarach,
that is needed for every utterance:
"My words which I have placed in your mouth";
and that there be preparation on man's part,
the expression of urging and the expression of affection;
and also that he attain humility and lowliness,
for words of Torah are compared to water:
just as water leaves a high place
and goes to a low place,
so too words of Torah endure only
in one whose mind is humble,
and "a sign of arrogance is poverty,"
And when one sees that a person attains lowliness,
it is a sign that it is
"My words which I have placed in your mouth,"
that he be a vessel ready to receive.

p: "One might think there was a calling even for the pauses;
the Torah says, 'and He spoke,' etc.;
and what purpose did the pauses serve?
Now this needs to be understood:
that there should be a calling for the pauses?
it says that the pauses served, etc.,
meaning that it should enter the heart.
And the essence of the words of Torah is:
"May He open our heart through His Torah
and place in our heart love of Him and fear of Him."
And this is why it says,
"One might think there was a calling for the pauses,"
meaning that this too came from Hashem Yisbarach's side;
for the speech there was a calling.
That is, the words of Torah
Hashem Yisbarach caused to shine forth from His side;
and this is why a calling preceded,
the expression which the ministering angels use,
"And one called to the other, etc."
allude to the holiness of the three Avos
"Holy in the heavens on high, etc."
corresponds to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him;
נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
corresponds to the holiness of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
"The lip of truth shall be established forever."
the traits of Avraham and Yitzchak,
אוּרִיאֵל נֶגֶד קְדֻשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and Uriel corresponds to the holiness of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him.
so that there shine forth in Knesses Yisrael
the holiness of the three Avos.
And through the calling, the expression of affection,
for the holiness of all the Avos is words of Torah:
with Avraham the words of Torah began:
"'Let there be light': this is Avraham"
and Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him:
"The Torah comes from the side of Gevurah"
and Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him:
so that it enter the heart,
"May He open our heart through His Torah":
that the words of Torah enter the heart
And Shabbos has in it an influx
that it corresponds to Malchus, the mouth;

inlineHeadings.text: Contemplation Brings Torah Into the Heart

paragraphs.text: Source: Yeshayahu 6:10 — “השמן לב העם הזה ואזניו הכבד ועיניו השע פן יראה בעיניו ובאזניו ישמע ולבבו יבין ושב ורפא לו” — “Dull that people’s mind, Stop its ears, And seal its eyes— Lest, seeing with its eyes And hearing with its ears, It also grasp with its mind, And repent and save itself.””

paragraphs.text: Source: Berachos 5b — “אמר ליה רבי יוחנן: בשלמא תורה וגמילות חסדים, דכתיב: ״בחסד ואמת יכפר עון״. ״חסד״ — זו גמילות חסדים, שנאמר: ״רודף צדקה וחסד ימצא חיים צדקה וכבוד״. ״אמת״ — זו תורה, …” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 42) — “Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him: What is your source for this? Granted, if one engages in Torah and acts of charity, his transgressions are forgiven, as it is written: “With mercy and truth, iniquity is expiated” (Proverbs 16:6); mercy refers to acts of charity, as it is stated: “He who pursues charity and mercy finds life, charity and honor” (Proverbs 21:21), mercy and charity are listed together. And truth refers to …”
